config.hero: a lamplighter who is afraid of the dark
config.setting: a walled city on the longest night of winter

bible.title: The Lamplighter of Coldbarrow
bible.premise: Armed only with a brass pole and a secret dread of the dark, you walk the freezing cobblestones of Coldbarrow on the longest night of winter. Someone or something is trailing your footsteps, snuffing out every lamp you kindle and leaving strange frost in the gutters.
bible.heart: Your clumsy stray hound relies entirely on you for warmth and safety, and he has bolted ahead into the freezing alleys where the shadows stir.
bible.goal: Reach and ignite the Great Lantern upon the North Gate to flood the entire walled borough with protective, golden light.
bible.danger: A spiteful saboteur stalks your steps through the fog, dousing every wick with icy water to plunge the city into supernatural gloom.
bible.world: Coldbarrow is a steep, walled fortress town of crooked slate roofs and iron lamp-posts fueled by thick amber tallow. On the longest night of the year, frost thickens unnaturally fast wherever light fades, and the cobbles echo with things that hate the flame. Safety relies entirely on the connected chain of streetlamps running from the river docks up to the towering North Gate.

characters.name: Agnes
characters.description: A sharp-eyed apothecary with stained cuffs who brews luminous glow-moss and wants to prove that the freezing gloom is an ancient alchemical vapor.

characters.name: Giles
characters.description: A retired city watchman with a brass ear-trumpet who wants a peaceful night and suspects the town council is hiding something in the tower.

characters.name: Kester
characters.description: A nimble chimney-sweeper with soot-dusted sleeves who wants to pry loose the Great Lantern's silver reflector to sell by morning.

characters.name: Maud
characters.description: A kind, sturdy baker whose communal brick oven has never gone out, wanting to keep her mother-ember alive against the unnatural frost.

rules: Any streetlamp left unlit for too long gathers a crust of unnatural blue frost.
Brass lamp housings must be fully latched against the draft or the cold fog snuffs the flame instantly.
Shadows that gather in deep darkness whisper secrets, but they scatter into smoke the moment tallow light touches them.
The Great Lantern atop the North Gate can illuminate the whole city at once, provided its brass mechanism is not frozen shut.

pages.text:
You tuck your woollen scarf tight around Barnaby’s shaggy neck, but your hound only shivers and licks your cold knuckles. He is a clumsy stray with floppy ears, and he counts on you to keep the dark away. You raise your brass pole and touch its glowing taper to the streetlamp at the corner of Weaver Street. The amber wick flares up, bright and warm.

A sharp hiss cuts through the silence. A splash of icy water douses the wick, and strange blue frost snaps across the iron glass. Barnaby gives a terrified yelp and bolts up the freezing alley toward the North Gate. From the shadows behind you, quick footsteps patter away into the fog.

choices.text: Chase after Barnaby into the pitch-black alley.
Stalk the hidden footsteps fading into the fog.

factsAdded.text: Barnaby bolted into the dark alley toward the North Gate.
A hidden saboteur snuffed the Weaver Street lamp with freezing water.

pages.illustrationPrompt: an iron streetlamp with a glowing amber flame

pages.choiceText: Chase after Barnaby into the pitch-black alley.
pages.text:
You plunge into the pitch-black alley, guided only by Barnaby's frantic whimpers. The freezing shadows whisper like dry leaves, but the tiny pilot flame on your pole holds them back. At the alley's bend, your light reveals your hound cowering beside a stranger in soot-dusted clothes.

The boy hops down from a rain-barrel, holding Barnaby safely by his collar. It is Kester, the chimney-sweep. "Quiet, boy," Kester whispers, wiping ash on his sleeve. "A cloaked figure just scurried past with a bucket of slush, dousing the lamps. I'm climbing to the North Gate myself. You can scramble up the roof ladders with me, or take the icy streets below—if you dare face what's prowling them."

choices.text: Trust Kester and climb the ladder to the rooftops.
Decline Kester's offer and stay on the street.

factsAdded.text: You reunited with Barnaby in the dark alley.
Kester revealed that a cloaked figure with slush is dousing lamps from the roofs.

pages.illustrationPrompt: A slight stranger in soot-dusted clothes crouching in an alley

pages.choiceText: Stalk the hidden footsteps fading into the fog.
pages.text:
You creep through the mist, following fresh footprints pressed into the blue frost. They lead around a sharp bend into Baker's Court, where the shadows huddle close. You raise your brass pole like a club, but the tracks end abruptly beneath an iron drainpipe.

"Looking for me, wick-tender?" whispers a voice overhead. A scrawny boy perches on the rain gutter. It is Kester, a nimble chimney-sweep with soot-dusted sleeves. He taps his brass scraper against the brickwork. "I saw who threw the freezing water. A fellow in a grey cowl, slipping toward the bakery. Take me up to the North Gate, and I'll help you catch him."

choices.text: Hurry to the bakery to confront the saboteur.
Climb toward the North Gate with Kester.

factsAdded.text: Kester the chimney-sweep offered to help in exchange for reaching the North Gate.
A saboteur in a grey cowl fled toward the bakery.

pages.illustrationPrompt: fresh footprints pressed into a crust of blue frost across cobblestones

pages.choiceText: Hurry to the bakery to confront the saboteur.
Climb toward the North Gate with Kester.
Trust Kester and climb the ladder to the rooftops.
pages.text:
You tuck Barnaby into Kester's sturdy soot-sack, sling him across your back, and scramble up the ladder. Up on the crooked slates, the wind bites hard. A trail of icy footprints gleams across the frost, leading straight toward the North Gate.

Barnaby pokes his nose out and growls. Ahead by a chimney, the cloaked figure tips a bucket of slush into a flue, sending up clouds of blue vapor. But Kester tugs your sleeve, showing off a brass crowbar. "Forget the meddler," Kester whispers. "Help me pry loose the Great Lantern's silver reflector, and we'll split the coin. Tallow light won't buy you breakfast."

choices.text: Confront the saboteur before they freeze the tower stairs.
Promise Kester the silver so he guides you past the ledges.

factsAdded.text: Kester plans to pry loose the Great Lantern's silver reflector.
You spotted the cloaked saboteur pouring freezing slush down a chimney flue.

pages.illustrationPrompt: A trail of icy footprints leading across frosty roof slates

pages.choiceText: Decline Kester's offer and stay on the street.
pages.text:
You shake your head. Barnaby has clumsy paws and no wings; slick slate roofs are no place for a hound. Kester shrugs and scrambles up a drainpipe into the dark eaves. "Watch your step, then," he calls down. A trail of wet footprints glistens on the stones, crusting over with pale blue frost.

You follow the tracks toward High Market. Around the corner, an old watchman crouches beside a dead lamp, aiming a brass ear-trumpet at an iron grating. It is Giles. "Hush your boots!" he grunts. "The council swore it was wind, but something down there is drinking the tallow dry."

Barnaby whines at the grating, but further up the hill, an iron bucket clatters on the steps toward the North Gate.

choices.text: Ask Giles what is lurking beneath the grating.
Rush uphill toward the clatter on the steps.

factsAdded.text: Giles suspects something beneath the street gratings is drinking the tallow.
You heard a bucket clatter on the steps to the North Gate.

pages.illustrationPrompt: a trail of wet footprints across freezing cobblestones

pages.choiceText: Ask Giles what is lurking beneath the grating.
pages.text:
"What is down there?" you ask, kneeling close.

Giles holds up a scarred hand for silence, his ear-trumpet pressed against the cold streetlamp. "Tallow-leeches," he rasps. "Nasty things that hate the heat. Someone opened the sewer sluice below, driving them up into the supply pipes to drink every wick in Coldbarrow dry."

Beneath the grating, a wet slithering stirs right under your boots. Barnaby barks once and cowers behind your woollen coat. Further up the winding stairs, an iron bucket clatters against stone. The saboteur is rushing straight for the Great Lantern atop the gate.

Giles brandishes an iron pry-bar. "Help me wedge this open and torch the pipe," he urges, "or the whole town goes dark."

choices.text: Help Giles pry open the iron grating.
Rush up the stairs after the saboteur.

factsAdded.text: Giles revealed that tallow-leeches are being driven up the pipes to drink the town's oil.

pages.illustrationPrompt: a dark iron streetlamp crusted with frost beside an old grating

pages.choiceText: Rush uphill toward the clatter on the steps.
pages.text:
You sprint up the steep stone staircase, Barnaby scrambling close at your heels. At the landing, an iron bucket lies overturned, spilling slush across the frosty flags. Just ahead, a hooded figure drops a dripping ladle and darts into an open cellar beneath the gatehouse.

A warm glow cuts through the fog from a nearby doorway. It is Maud, the baker, clutching an iron shovel heaped with glowing embers. "Lamplighter!" she whispers fiercely, shielding the heat with her apron. "The North Gate winch is freezing fast, and my oven coals won't survive this draft much longer."

Down in the dark cellar, stone steps groan under hurried boots.

choices.text: Carry Maud's embers up to the frozen gate winch.
Charge down into the dark cellar after the saboteur.

factsAdded.text: Maud has glowing embers to thaw the North Gate winch.
The saboteur fled into the gatehouse cellar.

pages.text:
You wedge the foot of your brass pole into the slot, heaving with all your might beside the old watchman. The iron grating pops open with a screech. Down in the conduit, bloated tallow-leeches squirm across the cracked pipes, shrinking from the yellow glow of your brass lantern.

"They're chewing through the gate's tallow line!" Giles rasps, fumbling with a flask of spirits. "Lend me your taper to burn them out, or the Great Lantern won't have a drop of fuel!"

Before you can strike a spark, Barnaby barks sharply and bolts up the North Gate stairs. High above, a hooded figure drops an empty pail and scrambles toward the summit.

choices.text: Burn the tallow-leeches with Giles before the pipes run dry.
Chase after Barnaby and the saboteur up the gate stairs.

factsAdded.text: The tallow-leeches are chewing through the North Gate's fuel supply pipe.
Barnaby bolted up the North Gate stairs after the saboteur.

pages.illustrationPrompt: A brass pole lantern shining light down into an open iron sewer grating.

pages.choiceText: Rush up the stairs after the saboteur.
pages.text:
You leave Giles to his pipe and take the steep stone staircase two steps at a time. Barnaby scrambles behind your heels, his claws clicking on the slick ice. High above, the North Gate looms against the freezing dark, dead and cold.

A shop door bangs open on the mid-way landing. A sharp-eyed woman with ink-stained cuffs steps into your path, thrusting a jar of luminous green moss at your chest. It is Agnes the apothecary.

"He kicked right through my stoop!" Agnes snaps, pointing up the steps. "That rogue carries brimstone frost. One drop in the Great Lantern's reservoir and the basin will shatter like cheap glass. Coat your pole with my moss to warm the oil, or run him down before he dumps it!"

choices.text: Take Agnes's glow-moss to protect the lamp reservoir.
Sprint past Agnes to tackle the saboteur immediately.

factsAdded.text: Agnes warned that the saboteur has brimstone frost to crack the Great Lantern's reservoir.
Agnes offered you a jar of luminous glow-moss.
